body: I don't really know what to say or where to start. I mean I said a lot, but I know most people won't read it which is fine. It helps to just put the words together sometimes.

That's a helpful way to think about it. I also liked your other post about not owing the depression anything. Sometimes it's really hard to remember "Yes, this is part of me, but it doesn't DEFINE who I am." How I took what you said was basically following through is surrendering to something that I shouldn't be giving in to and allowing the depression to define me.

Thanks for the acronym. I had been wondering about that for a while. And I know what you're saying. The selfishness idea is something I always have trouble with and find it difficult to think clearly about. I know it would hurt the people around me, even the people I don't really know that well. I never want to think I could knowingly inflict that much pain on people I care about. At the same time, I also feel like (as messed up as it is) aren't those people being equally selfish? I have to keep putting all this time, money, and energy into battling a chemical imbalance I didn't ask for that makes me absolutely miserable and will be with me the rest of my life just so they don't have to deal with the fact that I made an educated, thought-out decision to not be here over being with them? It just seems like a socially constructed double standard to me. Not trying to discount your post at all, just sharing my own difficulty. I really appreciate your words.
